description:
Sponsor: Crucial DDR5 Memory https://geni.us/XKQaQ
AMD's RX 7900 XT is basically just an upsell technique for the RX 7900 XTX. The XT fails to provide any meaningful value over last generation cards, it fails to beat any NVIDIA 40-series cards, and it is clearly a greedy play at pushing consumers to the RX 7900 XTX -- just like the 4080 is designed to push people to the 4090, except NVIDIA at least has the defense of being the literal 'best' on the charts. This review and benchmark of the AMD RX 7900 XT will test it vs. the RX 7900 XTX, the NVIDIA RTX 4080 and 4090, the AMD RX 6950 XT, and more. We're looking at gaming performance, ray tracing, thermals, and power.

Watch our AMD RX 7900 XTX review: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=We71eXwKODw
Watch our AMD RX 7900 XTX tear-down: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BMKK6z__tXM
RDNA3 GPU architecture deep-dive: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9iEDpXyFLFU

The best way to support our work is through our store: https://store.gamersnexus.net/

AMD:s 8k gaming wasn't 8k*4k display, it was the upcoming ultrawide displays, 8kx2k resolution instead of old ultrawides of 4kx1080p displays.  As for benefit of increasing resolution, older games and desktop applications don't require too much horsepower and benefit from higher resolution, and for newer stuff you can either turn down settings or resolution.
I'm using 2070 super with 4k TV. It isn't what reviewers would call a 4k gaming card, but its all about game selection. I do have to sacrifice quality or resolution in few games, but for majority that I play with it is perfect, the GPU fast enough to run and resolution helps more than faster GPU for strategy games and the kind of productivity that I do.  There's probably a time when I want to upgrade to 8k display that I can run at 60hz for low paced things,  and 4k 144hz for high paced games. And that's the beauty of improving support for higher resolutions you can take benefit where it benefits and ignore it when it's harmful on a same system.  After saying all this, I need Nvidia software developer tools so AMD isn't option for me.

As an average casual gamer, I hate the complexity of modern day GPU reviews, where they break down the charts into different game technologies like "RT on" vs "RT off", and the fact that games use bits and pieces of RT to a difference extent. comments.text:
Some more insight into why the 7900XT is a misleading name for this SKU. Traditionally the two ATI/AMD top end products were only separated by clock speeds when the price difference was around 10%. Memory bus width and shader/rop/tmu count always remained the same. 9700 and 9700 Pro, 9800 and 9800 Pro, X800XT and X800XT PE, X1900XT and X1900XTX, X1950XT and X1950XTX, HD2900 PRO vs HD2900 XT, HD3850 and HD3870, HD4870 and HD4890.

There only started to be a reduction in core config ratio after the 5000 series, along with a somewhat larger percentage difference in price, with the HD5850 and HD5870, HD6950 and HD6970, HD7950 vs HD7970, R9 290/390 and 290X/390X, RX 470-570/480-580, Vega 56/64, 5700/5700XT etc. but the memory bus and capacity remained pretty much the same across the two SKUs. Even the 6800XT and 6900XT stuck to this formula. Now though, the 7900XT makes no sense because both the core and the memory configuration is cut down while only offering a 10% reduction in price. Makes no sense whatsoever.

For reviewers claiming to have 9 years of experience you missed two important aspects:
- the amplitude of the Xs are important too. While NVIDIA supplies an amplitude of only 4090 for its one X, AMD cards manage to go as high as 7900 for up to 5 Xs.
- from the perspective of symmetry, AMDs RX 7900 XT takes the lead with perfectly balanced positioning of the Xs around the amplitude. The cards with odd numbers of Xs all suffer from asymmetric positioning. While NVIDIAs RTX 4090 is slanted to the left on par with XFXs' flagship with respect to the number of Xs, the AMD RX 7900 XTX is the only card that manages to position more Xs to the right of the amplitude. The gap between the XFX RX 7900 XTX (5 Xs) and AMD RX 7900 XTX certainly leaves room to fit in another card with symmetric positioning (XRX 7900 XTX upcoming?).
Personally, I am not sure why both card producers decided to not put Xs in the amplitude when using an odd number of Xs. Maybe there are technical reasons to favor an asymmetric positioning?

Despite all the people crying about Nvidia price-performance, they are actually targeting performance where they believe it matters most - a future where ray tracing(and AI) is commonly used. 

Ironically, while it's cheaper than the competition, I don't see many people rushing out to buy AMD's $1000 card for the sake of its raster performance, either. Last-gen cards ALREADY check that box, at much cheaper prices. 

While I still believe Nvidia dropped the ball with pricing, I thoroughly believe their vision for the future of games is on point. Price cuts will come, and lower-end cards will launch, but the architectural vision for these round of GPUs is already set in stone. So, beteen these two makers, AMD is actually in the more precarious position, especially as  next-gen games begin saturate the market.

The 7900-XTX is the kind* of card AMD needed... 2 generations ago, when raster performance was the be-all-end-all of real-time rendering. A new race has started, and AMD is barely in it!

comments.text:
@legros731  the XTX is disappointing because AMD claimed it would come with a 50-70% performance increase compared to the 6950 XT. I didn’t expect it to get anywhere near the 4090. Anyone who expected that was out of their mind. 

Nvidia’s reference cooler design for the 40 series is insanely effective. Those cards barely heat up at all. They run well within comfortably temps and are more power efficient than any of AMD’s cards, despite efficiency being one of AMD’s main marketing points. AMD made a nice looking reference design but it apparently has wicked coil whine in some cases, runs fairly hot and pulls a lot of power.  

I’m far from being some kind of Nvidia fanboy. I had high hopes for the 7900 series. And I think that AMD will likely be able to squeeze a bit more performance out of them with driver optimizations but when it comes to delivering on what they claimed, they just didn’t. The difference between the 6950 XT and the 7900 XTX was sometimes as low as 15-25%. Nowhere near the 50-70% improvement that AMD boasted about. The prices for the 7900 XT and XTX cards are way too high for what the cards are currently capable of. End of story. Even if the XTX does squeak past the 4080 in most games, that doesn’t mean the $1,000-1,300 price tag is justified. It just means that AMD and Nvidia are both capitalizing on the fact that a lot of rubes are willing to seriously overpay for mediocre performance improvements, most likely because they’re worried that if they don’t overpay for one now, they may not get another chance to buy one. If AMD had made the XTX 60-70% more powerful than the 6950 XT, then maybe I’d be more accepting of the price they’ve set but realistically, the 4080 should be an $800 card and the XTX should probably be around $700-750. Both of them are $300-400 more expensive than they should be. 

And how about that launch? The entire stock sold out within an hour or two tops, sites weren’t working properly, there weren’t nearly enough cards to meet demand and scalpers started listing them on eBay for $1,500-1,800. I’m sure some people were stupid enough to pay that much too.

comments.text:
Nvidia needs to stop acting stupid and reduce the price of their 4080.  They have a chance to give AMD's discreet GPU business a knockout punch.  And no, I'm not suggesting that they would totally put them out of business, but they have a golden opportunity to do MASSIVE DAMAGE to AMD's discreet GPU business this generation.  A 4080 at $1,000 MSRP is a choice that most people would absolutely make over a $1,000 7900XTX.  The 7900XTX may have an extremely small performance advantage at 4K resolution, but it's very, very small and varies by game, and by going with Nvidia's 4080 you are getting a card with dramatically better drivers AND dramatically better RT performance if that matters to you.

At a $900 MSRP, the 4080 would BURY AMD.  It would completely demolish them.  Only a truly brain-dead fanboy clown would buy EITHER AMD card (the 7900XTX or the worthless trash XT) over a $900 4080.  That price point would put this 7900XT right into the dumpster where it belongs.  What a trash card this thing is.  Nvidia is going to be making plenty of money off of the 4090 because its performance increase over the best AMD could manage this gen is ABSOLUTELY MASSIVE.  It is the one and only card that true enthusiast gamers who are playing everything at 4K resolution will buy.  I'm waiting for my opportunity to get one to replace my 3090.

So with Nvidia making bank on the only truly "premium" (from a performance standpoint) GPU of this generation (Nvidia literally might not even release a 4090 Ti because AMD has absolutely no chance of even coming close to the 4090's performance), they have a chance to slightly reduce the price of their 4080 and just totally bury AMD.  Nvidia not only has the performance crown by a giant margin this gen with their 4090, but they also have a HUGE efficiency advantage as well.  And you'll notice that last gen the AMD fanboy's go-to excuse was "Nvidia is making 500-watt space heaters and AMD is so much more efficient!", but now I have seen NONE of the AMD fanboys even MENTIONING energy efficiency because Nvidia now as the efficiency crown as well.

Nvidia just crushed AMD this gen, and I will be interested to see if Jensen is smart enough to take advantage of the massive performance and efficiency advantage that they have over AMD right now by reducing the price of the 4080 to either $1,000 or $900 and delivering a total knockout punch to AMD's discreet graphics business.

comments.text:
When you get to the halo products the people who buy them tend to be affluent enough that these prices aren't really prohibitive. They also tend to feel a need to have the latest and greatest just because it's available. The real enthusiasts who does have a tighter budget usually try to upgrade every other generation or even shop for last gen halo products.

Even i f the halo cards cost twice or three times as much there would be some buyers who had to have one if just to be able to say so. Cost / benefit isn't something that means anything when you get this far away from the mainstream. Someone recently reminded me about an app for the iPhone. There was an app released and available on the app store that had no other function than to show you was rich enough to buy it. It was the very aptly named "I am Rich!" app. It showed a red ruby on the screen and it cost $999.99 back in 2008. There were actually a few who bought it at that price, though most of them applied for a refund and Apple decided to remove the app and refund all buyers. Still there were some who actually bought it just because they could...

If you were to try to get a good cost/benefit ratio for everything then there's a lot of things that wouldn't exist. Car brands like Ferrari, Lamborghini Spyker and all the other super and hyper car manufacturers simply wouldn't have a market, and yet they are still selling ever more ridiculously priced cars.

My point is that when they get expensive enough even graphics cards become status symbols and people will pay for that.
